newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Fund-raising porridge for Philippines plebiscite.
newsitem.headline: Fund-raising porridge for Philippines plebiscite.

text.p: A Filipino group raising funds for a campaign to allow President Fidel Ramos to stand for a second term in office will sell porridge at 1,000 pesos ($38) a bowl, organisers said on Saturday.

The group, the People's Initiative for Reforms, Modernisation and Action (PIRMA), needs to gather five million signatures to force a plebiscite on a change in constitutional laws, which restrict the president to a single term.

Ramos, who was elected president for six years in 1992, has said he will not stand for office again, but has rejected opposition calls to put his pledge in writing. He has said he has no link with PIRMA.
PIRMA organisers said they will sell porridge at 1,000 pesos a bowl at the Via Mare restaurant in Manila's Makati district on Saturday night to raise funds for their campaign.
A manager at the restaurant said 300 bowls of rice porridge, flavoured with slices of pork and beancurd, had been prepared. The dish is listed on the menu at 85 pesos ($3.23), he said.

PIRMA, which is led by former diplomat Alberto Pedrosa and his wife Carmen, has said economic reforms initiated by Ramos are in danger of losing steam if Ramos is not re-elected in 1998. But the country's powerful Roman Catholic church has opposed allowing Ramos to stand for a second term on the grounds that it could lead to a dictatorship.

Two of the country's leading business groups, the Makati Business Club and the Management Association of the Philippines, have said amending the constitution could send negative signals to foreign investors.
